answer: Tidal terrace attestation: identities register only through a physical sensor terrace on a shoreline, logging continuous wave-phase readings that vary by location and time. An ocean buoy verifies each claim against its own sensors. Because wave phase at a given terrace drifts unpredictably, a single operator cannot fabricate matching readings for many identities without deploying separate physical sensors at distinct locations. Each fake identity thus costs a real sensor plus maintenance, and a glacier-fed site is required to prevent replay.
